session_overhead_decomposition.note: These percentages are estimated from the S371 capacity model (30% automation-reducible overhead) and observed session patterns. A session of 20 items at ~8 hours total allocates approximately 3.6h to content creation, 2.4h to governance, 0.6h to backups, 0.4h to defect scans, 0.6h to quality review, and 0.4h to documentation.

capacity_model_ceiling.source: S861 demonstrated 25 Analyze via stem rewrite (Pathway A, 5.0 items/hr net). Net-new authoring (Pathway B) is capped at 20 due to Evaluate complexity.
capacity_model_ceiling.evaluate_bottleneck: Evaluate items are 1/hr each. A 20-item wave with 8 Evaluate items takes 8h for Evaluate alone. This is the binding constraint for 3-wave/week sustainability.

risk_factors: Session-overlap collision risk: 2 waves/week → 2 independent write sessions, each reading file state. S56-S58 precedent shows parallel sessions consume each other's target slots without coordination.
Governance overhead doubles: T0 hash verification, registry reconciliation, and Tmid/Tend checkpoint sequences run twice per week. At 30% overhead per session, 2 waves = 4.8h of governance per week.
Evaluate bottleneck persists: At 8 Evaluate items/wave, 381 needed = 47.6 waves @ 2/week = ~24 weeks. Evaluate items cannot be accelerated through automation.
Reviewer fatigue: 2 review sessions/week with governance checkpointing at T0/Tmid/Tend per session (AGENTS.md §13.1) — sustained over 20+ weeks this strains single-reviewer capacity.
File-size impact: Pack C (1.9MB) and Pack D (2.0MB) require Function constructor parse for each session. Parse time scales with file size — 2 sessions/week doubles this cost.
mitigation_strategies: Stagger wave timing to avoid same-day parallel sessions
Pre-allocate QID slots to prevent slot collision (S56-S58 fix)
Two-tier certification reduces review burden ~12% for Analyze-only items

risk_factors: Slot collision becomes near-certain: 3 concurrent write windows per week reading from the same 2 pack files. S56-S58 collision was at 2 sessions in one day — 3 sessions/week amplifies this risk by 3x.

Governance overhead accumulates non-linearly: T0 hash verification of 13 files at each session startup, Tmid at ~30 min, Tend with full reconciliation. At 3 sessions/week, this consumes ~7.2h in governance alone — more than the productive content work.

Context loss between sessions: Each wave requires full pack file re-read + Function constructor parse + state verification. Pack files are ~1.8-2.0MB each. Parsing 1.9MB of JavaScript objects 3x/week adds non-trivial compute overhead.

Evaluate bottleneck becomes binding: At 8 Evaluate/wave × 3 waves = 24 Evaluate/week theoretical, but actual yields ~18/week due to rework and slot contention. 381 needed = 21 weeks of pure Evaluate work. Impossible to sustain at the demonstrated ~1 Evaluate/hr design rate.

Backup protocol overhead: 3 sessions × 2 pack files × timestamped backups = 6 backup operations/week. Each backup copies ~2MB × 2 = ~4MB of data. With verification (hash check post-backup), this is ~15 min/week just for backup operations.

Multi-agent orchestration decay: Each session using 3+ parallel agents requires reconciliation of agent outputs. At 3 sessions/week, agent-output conflict rate increases because agents read stale file states.

Reviewer fatigue at 3x: 41-week program at 1 wave/week is already HIGH fatigue risk (S374). At 3 waves/week compressed to 14 weeks, the per-session review intensity triples — more defects per session, less time for each review.
REVISION_HISTORY.md write contention: One file, written at the end of every session. At 3 writes/week, append-order integrity requires serialization that defeats parallel-wave execution.
mitigation_strategies: Dedicated Evaluate workstream (Condition F from S374) — decouple Analyze and Evaluate into separate parallel tracks
Automation package (Condition C from S374): Reduce clerical overhead by 30%, freeing 4h/week for productive work
Strict slot pre-allocation: Assign QID ranges to waves before any writes, preventing slot collision entirely
Domain rotation: Assign different pack sections to different waves to reduce file contention (e.g., W1=Pack C EC, W2=Pack D FD, W3=Pack C FC)
Two-tier certification: Production tier for Analyze items cuts review time ~20%
Pipeline artifact reuse (C2 from S374/DL-036): Pass pre-computed state between pipeline stages instead of re-parsing files

recommendation.rationale: 2 waves/week (40 items/week) is the maximum sustainable rate given current governance architecture. At 3 waves/week, governance overhead (~7.2h/week) exceeds productive content work (~10.8h/week), creating a net-negative efficiency ratio. The S56-S58 parallel-session collision (15 slots consumed, requiring adaptive slot selection) proves that 2 independent write sessions on the same pack files already produce contention. Three waves would compound this risk exponentially. Additionally, the Evaluate bottleneck (1 item/hr design rate, 381 needed) cannot be accelerated by increasing wave frequency — it requires a dedicated parallel workstream (S374 Condition F), not more waves.
conditions_for_2_waves_sustainability: 1. File-lock protocol implemented: No two sessions may write to the same pack file within the same calendar day (DL-019 prevention).
2. Slot pre-allocation: Assign specific QID ranges to each wave AB initio. Wave 1 gets EC slots, Wave 2 gets ED slots — no overlap.
3. Automation package deployed: Reduce governance overhead from 30% → 21% (S374 Condition C).
4. Two-tier certification adopted: Analyze items (80%) get Production-tier review (12% time savings), Evaluate items (20%) retain Gold-tier (no savings).
5. Dedicated Evaluate workstream: Launch as parallel non-wave-gated track per S374 Condition F. Evaluate throughput increases independently of wave frequency.
6. Domain rotation: Waves operate on different pack/section combinations to minimize file-lock contention.
conditions_for_3_waves_if_mandated: A. Full pipeline artifact reuse: Upstream stages produce pre-computed parse results. Downstream stages consume artifacts, not raw files (DL-036 fix). Eliminates 2 of 3 T0 hash verification sessions per week.
B. Evaluate workstream fully decoupled and running 2x/week independently — not gated by wave frequency.
C. Automation deployed and verified for 3 consecutive weeks before ramp to 3 waves.
D. File write windows scheduled non-overlapping: e.g., Monday AM, Wednesday AM, Friday AM — each separated by ≥24 hours.
E. Governance guard upgraded to enforce slot-lock: Rules 2/5/6/9 expanded to check for QID ownership across sessions.
F. REVISION_HISTORY.md batched: Append entries once per week (3-session batch) rather than per-session — reduces serialization bottleneck.
recommendation.s374_alignment: S374 concluded 'Expansion AUTHORIZATION reachable at 1 wave/week in ~6-8 weeks. Expansion EXECUTION NOT viable at 1 wave/week.' This throughput analysis confirms: 2 waves/week is the minimum viable execution rate, and 3 waves/week is required for the 14-week cognitive gap closure target but carries HIGH sustainability risk that can only be mitigated by the 6 conditions above.
